candidate_binding: Source and complete production-class hashes below; local commit created after validation.
objective: Reduce real recipe executions through bounded supplemental proposals; retain the previously certified incumbent when optional work cannot improve it.

implementation.ordering: After all existing route, small-batch and terminal searches.
implementation.proposal: Change one active producer of the first full-inventory free policy; reuse its upstream choices, exactly evaluate the resulting fixed material DAG, then confirm with the existing planner.
safety: Full stock snapshot restored only for the supplemental candidates.
Saved execution bound is the validated full-inventory Search bound, not the later capped-stock bound.
No byproducts, stateful inputs or private reusable-stock usage in the new phase.
Existing strict improvement, inventory and execution checks remain authoritative.
External cancellation propagates; optional cutoff retains the last complete certificate.

limitations: The deterministic ordinary DAG grid is not a modpack frequency estimate.
All firings are real recipes; no synthetic tags or stateful inputs occur.
Global execution minima use the original finite full inventory.
This audit contains no performance measurements.

exact_vanilla.scope: All ancestors of the eight supplied Vanilla targets, preserving every mixed tag-member input allocation; not the full Vanilla graph.

performance.order: AB/BA alternation inside each matched pair, complete isolated production classloaders in each JVM
performance.timing_scope: CraftPlannerV2.planDetailed only. Existing graph and stock reused; preparation, validation, reflection, JSON, class loading and JVM startup excluded.
performance.heap_scope: Allocated bytes is total per-request thread allocation, not retained heap, RSS or peak memory.
performance.statistical_scope: Four-fork descriptive medians/ranges and per-fork nearest-rank p95; no confidence/significance claim from this small fork count.
performance.interpretation: The improved examples take fewer recipe executions at modest additional planning CPU/allocation cost. This is not a claim of general planning speedup or server TPS improvement.

rejected_experiment.variant: Strictly fewer executions without the existing 1% gain threshold
rejected_experiment.decision: Supplemental search follows the existing 1% significant execution-gain threshold. The final candidate retains the baseline result for this case.
rejected_experiment.scope: The raw adapter counts synthetic tag conversions as firings. The 1% gate limits marginal rerouting cost; it does not fix or align that artificial objective. Physical execution claims use the exact external adapter.

limitations: This bounded single-producer neighborhood does not enumerate all mixed integer route combinations.
The original-order ordinary grid retains six execution gaps and one missed feasible case; reverse order retains eight gaps and the same missed feasible case.
Vanilla target 97 / leaves / amount 100000 still needs a mixed tail batch outside this neighborhood.
Existing raw-corpus budget cutoffs remain cutoffs, not mathematical infeasibility certificates.
Large-pack tag expansion was declined when exact mixed-member enumeration exceeded the external adapter cap; no member choices were silently removed.
No live Minecraft TPS or machine-duration measurements were performed.
